title: First music remembered: Buddy 'King' Boland's band
summary: Adams recalls King Boland, a cornetist with a dozen-piece band, famous among white and colored audiences.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Now, did your folks, your father play any instrument? Never did. Your mother, was she a singer or anything? No, never was. What was the first music you remember hearing when you were a little boy? Can you remember any? When I was a little boy, it was King Boland.
King Boland. What kind of a band did he have? Well, King Boland used to play a cornet, I think it was. Yeah. Yeah, he used to play a cornet. Called him King Boland.
Remember how big a band he had? Was it a big band, the little women?
Yeah, it was a big band. It was a good size band, I think. He had somewhere around between a dozen men in it.
How did he compare with the other bands?

That, I don't know. But he was tops at that time. Famous. They were white and colored. He was famous at that time. Buddy Boland. We used to call him King Boland. We used to call him King Boland, and his name was Buddy Boland at that time.
Do you know about where he lived?
What part of town? No, I didn't know where Buddy lived, but I knew he lived uptown there somewhere around. Uptown above McCoyland Avenue, around the other way, but whereabouts I didn't know.
